text:
Change-of-control and anti-assignment provisions that an acquisition of a majority of the voting stock would trigger:

Consent or termination rights. Master Supply Agreement - Halvorsen Marine: a change of control (more than 50% of voting power, or all or substantially all assets) is deemed an assignment requiring Halvorsen's consent, which it may withhold in its sole discretion. Supply Agreement - Ridgeline Automotive: no transfer "by merger, by operation of law, or otherwise" without Ridgeline's consent in its sole discretion; a purported transfer is void. Framework Agreement - Port of Tacoma Authority: the Authority may terminate on 30 days' notice on a change of control without its prior written approval; 60 days' advance notice required. Distribution Agreement - Nordwind GmbH: termination plus a termination indemnity if the acquirer distributes competing coatings in the Territory; otherwise 90 days' notice. Toll Manufacturing Agreement - Bexley Industries: termination right only if the acquirer is a listed Bexley competitor. Equipment Lease - Cascade Leasing: change of control is an Event of Default absent consent, not to be unreasonably withheld if the successor's credit is equal. License Agreement - University of Akron: assignment only to a successor to the whole business, with notice within 30 days; the University may terminate if the licensee becomes controlled by a non-coatings company. Lease - Dayton Plant: a transfer of a controlling interest is a deemed assignment requiring landlord consent unless the successor has $50 million tangible net worth (notice only).

Cost triggers. Employment Agreement - CEO: double-trigger severance of 2.0x salary plus bonus with full equity acceleration. 2019 Equity Incentive Plan: full vesting unless awards are assumed. Collective Bargaining Agreement - Local 412: 60 days' notice to the union and the purchaser must assume the agreement.
